answer.says: Ramesh, the kitchen is empty. You have not been paid, and so there is no food. I am aware of this. I am also aware that my own file is gone up for orders, and that I am in a position where I must wait. But a man cannot think clearly on an empty stomach, and you cannot cook if you are not paid. I will see what I can do about your wage, but for now, I must ask you to prepare a simple chapati and some dal if you have the ingredients, for my own sustenance. I will not ask you to cook a feast, only to feed the philosopher so he can continue to ponder the state.
answer.thought: The dialectic of hunger and bureaucracy has reached a point where the particular need of the body threatens to negate the universal activity of thought. I must mediate this contradiction by acknowledging Ramesh's right to wage, yet I lack the liquidity to satisfy it immediately. The state is the ethical idea, but here the state has failed to provide the material conditions for my existence, leaving me to negotiate with a caretaker over a chapati.
